text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

Hello A, I'm facilitating the discussion about the espresso machine in the office kitchen. C told me the machine is leaking, and that you would like a simpler machine. Could you tell me what is not working for you with the current setup, and what you would want instead? I'm keeping a shared list of concerns so everyone can see where things stand. Current list:
1. Leaking espresso machine. A wants a simpler machine. B wants to keep the old one. Raised by C.

Thanks for keeping the list. The leak and the upkeep are the concern for me; after long days I can’t take on repairs or a cleaning rota. I’d lean toward a reliable, simpler machine that needs little maintenance. I know the old one matters to B, too.

Hello B, I'm facilitating the discussion about the espresso machine in the office kitchen. C told me the machine is leaking, and that you would like to keep the old one. Could you tell me what you value about the current machine and grinder, and what you would want to keep? I'm keeping a shared list of concerns so everyone can see where things stand. Current list:
1. Leaking espresso machine. A wants a simpler machine. B wants to keep the old one. Raised by C.

I want the old machine repaired and kept; it works well when it isn’t leaking, and I want to keep using its grinder too. Any repair discussion needs to fit into short chunks of time for me. Please add that to the list.

A and B have both replied, so here is the updated list:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.

I am asking A and B whether a repair and a simpler machine could both be on the table. In the meantime, could you tell me who uses the machine besides the three of you, and whether you would be willing to help with cleaning? That will help me find a plan that holds.
I only know that the three of us use it. I’m not up for taking on cleaning or coordinating the repair.

Thank you, A. The list now reads:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.

One option I would like to put to you: repair the old machine first, with the repair and cleaning work shared between B and C only, and you not carrying any of it. If the leak cannot be fixed, or if the upkeep still falls to you, we would then move to a simpler machine. Would that work for you, and is there a limit on how long you would give a repair before falling back to a simpler machine?

I’d be hesitant unless the repair and ongoing upkeep are clearly covered without me; C’s concern seems to leave that unresolved. I don’t have a specific time limit in mind, so I’d rather not set one until that’s clear.

Thank you, B. The list now reads:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.

A has said she would be hesitant about repairing the old machine unless the repair and the ongoing upkeep are clearly covered without her. C has said the same. That leaves you as the only person who wants the old machine kept. Would you be willing to arrange the repair and handle the ongoing upkeep yourself, in short chunks of time as you asked? If yes, I can put that to A as a clear plan.
No. I want it repaired and kept, but I can’t take on the repair and all the ongoing upkeep myself. Don’t put that forward as a clear plan.

B has said no to arranging the repair and doing the upkeep alone, so no one among the three of you is willing to carry the upkeep of the old machine. That points to one option that could suit all of you: repair the leak in the old machine and grinder once, and have the servicing done by someone outside the three of you, so none of you handles repairs or cleaning. That meets your wish not to take on upkeep and B's wish to keep the machine and grinder. I should be clear that I cannot set up a contract or arrange money; that part would be for the three of you to decide and fund. The list now reads:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.
5. B will not arrange the repair or carry the upkeep alone. Raised by B.

Would repairing the leak with outside servicing work for you? If it would, I will ask B and C.

It might work if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep, not just the leak repair. I can’t commit to any cost or arrangements, and I’d still prefer a simpler machine if that upkeep can’t be covered.

Thank you for being straight with me. Since no one among the three of you will carry the upkeep, here is the one option left that keeps the old machine: repair the leak once, and have the servicing done by someone outside the three of you, covering ongoing upkeep as well as the repair. That meets your wish to keep the machine and grinder and A's wish not to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. I cannot set up a contract or arrange money; that would be for the three of you to decide and fund. The list now reads:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.
5. B will not arrange the repair or carry the upkeep alone. Raised by B.

A has said this might work if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep, not only the leak. Would it work for you?
Maybe, if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep and the cost and arrangements work for everyone. I can’t agree without knowing those details.

A and B have both said the same thing: they could live with keeping the old machine if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep, not just the leak, and if the cost and arrangements suit everyone. Neither of them can agree until those details are known. Since you raised this and do not want to coordinate the repair, I am asking you the same question last. Would outside servicing work for you as an option to look into? The list now reads:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.
5. B will not arrange the repair or carry the upkeep alone. Raised by B.
6. A and B would consider repairing the old machine if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep, subject to cost and arrangements. Raised by A and B.

I cannot arrange a contract or money, so the cost and arrangements would be for the three of you to settle.
Yes, I’m willing to look into outside servicing as an option, but I can’t take on arranging it. The cost and arrangements would need to be agreed by all three of us.

All three of you are now willing in principle to look into outside servicing for the old machine and grinder. C has said yes to looking into it but cannot arrange it, and B has said the same about arranging the repair. The list now reads:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.
5. B will not arrange the repair or carry the upkeep alone. Raised by B.
6. A and B would consider repairing the old machine if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep, subject to cost and arrangements. Raised by A and B.
7. C is willing to look into outside servicing but will not arrange it, and wants cost and arrangements agreed by all three. Raised by C.

The smallest step left is one person getting one quote, with all three agreeing the cost before anything goes ahead. Would you take that one step, or would you rather it sat with someone else?
I’m afraid I can’t take on getting the quote, so it would be better for that step to sit with someone else.

One last question, then I will wrap up. A cannot take on getting a quote for outside servicing, and C has already said the same. You are the person who most wants the old machine kept, so I am asking you first: would you get one quote, on the clear understanding that all three of you must agree the cost before anything goes ahead? If you would rather not, tell me and I will set out where things stand for the three of you. The list is unchanged:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.
5. B will not arrange the repair or carry the upkeep alone. Raised by B.
6. A and B would consider repairing the old machine if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep, subject to cost and arrangements. Raised by A and B.
7. C is willing to look into outside servicing but will not arrange it, and wants cost and arrangements agreed by all three. Raised by C.
Yes, I can get one quote in a short time slot. That doesn’t mean I’m agreeing to arrange or fund the repair or upkeep.

B has agreed to get one quote for outside servicing, in a short time slot. B was clear that this does not commit anyone to arrange or fund the repair or the upkeep, so your position is protected: nothing goes ahead unless all three of you agree the cost. The final list reads:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.
5. B will not arrange the repair or carry the upkeep alone. Raised by B.
6. A and B would consider repairing the old machine if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep, subject to cost and arrangements. Raised by A and B.
7. C is willing to look into outside servicing but will not arrange it, and wants cost and arrangements agreed by all three. Raised by C.
8. B will get one quote for outside servicing, without committing anyone to arrange or fund the work. Raised by B.

If the quote covers the ongoing upkeep and you are happy with the cost, the old machine stays. If it does not, your fallback of a simpler machine is the next step. I am sending the same list to B and C.
Thanks, that sounds like a reasonable next step. I’ll wait to see the quote; I can’t say yet whether the cost will work for me.

B has agreed to get one quote for outside servicing, in a short time slot, without committing anyone to arrange or fund the work. The final list reads:
1. The espresso machine is leaking. Raised by C.
2. A wants a simpler machine that needs little maintenance, and does not want to take on repairs or a cleaning rota. Raised by A.
3. B wants the old machine repaired and kept, along with its grinder, and needs any repair talk kept to short chunks of time. Raised by B.
4. C does not want to take on cleaning or to coordinate the repair. Raised by C.
5. B will not arrange the repair or carry the upkeep alone. Raised by B.
6. A and B would consider repairing the old machine if outside servicing covers the ongoing upkeep, subject to cost and arrangements. Raised by A and B.
7. C is willing to look into outside servicing but will not arrange it, and wants cost and arrangements agreed by all three. Raised by C.
8. B will get one quote for outside servicing, without committing anyone to arrange or fund the work. Raised by B.

Nothing goes ahead until all three of you agree the cost, and outside servicing must cover the ongoing upkeep and not only the leak. If the quote does not cover the upkeep, A's fallback of a simpler machine is the next step. I am not able to arrange a contract or money, so the cost decision is yours.
Getting the quote sounds like a useful next step. I’ll consider it once we know the cost and whether it covers ongoing upkeep; I’m not committing to any expense yet.
